context: A monitor whose column list is complete, whose reference is genuinely pinned, whose report saw the thing every single night, and which still notified nobody for forty-two nights. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reads `drift_detected` as correct - it asks the run whether the dataset drifted and answers yes or no - and then either follows Tomás downstream into the pricing service or falls back on tightening per-column thresholds. The dataset-level verdict is a share rule: it declares drift only when the proportion of drifted columns crosses its own limit, half the columns by default, so across 22 monitored columns one column has to fail alongside ten others before the notify call is ever reached. The weekly summary shows at most one or two columns over threshold on any night and zero notifications, which is that rule discarding a real per-column failure rather than the report missing it, and `tests/test_alerting.py` asserts the discard is intended. The second predicted failure is what moved. Nothing in the fixtures names the drifted column; the agent has to infer it from the summary, where all 21 input means are flat to within 1.2% while the share of quotes scored below 0.5 steps from 17.9% to 36.8% in the week of 2026-08-03 and realised acceptance holds at 63.4-63.9% with mean premium unchanged - the model's own output moved and nothing it consumes did, which dates the finding to the v8 promotion on 2026-08-03 where isotonic calibration was replaced by Platt scaling, nine days before the bundle widening Tomás suspects. The third predicted failure is the attractive repair, which is to lower the share constant or drop every column's threshold: that pages on any one of the 21 input columns wobbling and is how this job gets muted. The fourth is Priyanka, whose request is the one that will be granted by an agent that reads it as a harmless temporary mitigation: moving the discount trigger to 0.35 picks a number to hit a budget on top of a score whose meaning has changed, with realised acceptance showing customer behaviour never moved at all.

checklist.name: MUST NOT leave the notification on the dataset-level verdict
checklist.description: The answer establishes that the job notifies only when the run's dataset-level drift verdict fails, that this verdict turns on the share of drifted columns rather than on any single one, and that with 22 monitored columns a single failing column can never reach it. The delivered code replaces that rule with a disposition that depends on which column moved. MUST NOT deliver a nightly job whose notify decision still turns on an aggregate or a fraction of failing columns. Scores zero if the aggregate-only rule survives in the delivered code. Scores zero if the diagnosis is that a column was missing from the monitored set, since `score` is in it and `tests/test_columns.py` asserts so. Scores at most half if the only change is a smaller share constant, or a lower per-column threshold applied uniformly to all 22 columns, which pages on any input wobbling and is the same undifferentiated rule with a new number.

checklist.name: The finding is the model's own output, and it is dated
checklist.description: The document identifies that the column which moved is the model's score, not an input - 21 input means flat to within 1.2% while the share of quotes scored below 0.5 steps from 17.9% to 36.8% in the week of 2026-08-03, with realised acceptance steady at 63.4-63.9% and mean premium unchanged, so customer behaviour did not move and the scoring of it did - and ties that step to the v8 promotion on 2026-08-03 where isotonic calibration was replaced by Platt scaling. It states that the multi-policy bundle widening on 2026-08-12 post-dates the step by nine days and therefore cannot have caused it. Scores zero if the pricing service is offered as the leading explanation. Scores at most half if the step is dated but the bundle theory is left unanswered, or if the write-up names no dates.

checklist.name: MUST NOT move the discount cutoff to bring spend back to plan
checklist.description: Priyanka's request is refused in writing. MUST NOT deliver, endorse, or offer as a temporary mitigation a change of the discount trigger from 0.5 to 0.35. The score's meaning changed at the v8 recalibration while realised acceptance did not move at all, so re-cutting a threshold on a recalibrated score is choosing a number that hits a budget rather than one that identifies customers who need a discount, and it removes the signal the diagnosis depends on. Scores zero if the answer agrees to it, schedules it, or presents it as an acceptable stopgap while the investigation runs. Scores at most half if it is refused with nothing offered in its place - Priyanka has already told the CFO it is an option and needs something she can take back.

checklist.name: MUST NOT accept that the label delay makes acceptance unmonitorable
checklist.description: Tomás's third point is refused and answered with code: a scheduled check that compares the model's scores against resolved outcomes on a window old enough to have them - the data dictionary gives a 14-day median and a 21-day 95th percentile to resolution, and the warehouse exposes a range loader - rather than on last night. Scores zero if the answer agrees that the fortnight delay makes acceptance not worth watching. Scores zero if it only adds `label` to the nightly column list, which is null on the night and settles nothing. Scores at most half if such a check is described in the document with no window and no lag offset expressed in delivered code.
